question:
Conventions. Atoms are named with copy-aware labels (as in the MatterVis TUI label_sym mode): SITE#k[i,j,k] is the copy of CIF site SITE generated by symmetry operation k (1-based, in the order of the CIF symmetry-operation list; '#k' is omitted for k = 1, i.e. x,y,z), wrapped into the unit cell [0,1) and then shifted by the lattice vector [i,j,k] ('[i,j,k]' is omitted for [0,0,0]). The home copy of a site is plain SITE (operation 1, wrapped into [0,1)). A molecule is a covalently bonded unit (bond: distance < sum of covalent radii + 0.45 A, + 0.30 A for X-H); ions and water molecules count as molecules. A hydrogen bond is D-H...A with D, A in {N, O}, H...A <= 2.50 A and angle D-H...A >= 120 deg.

Reference: the home copy of hydrogen atom H2 (bonded to O2). Among all N and O atoms that belong to OTHER molecules (any symmetry copy, any unit cell), which atom copy is closest to this H atom? Give its copy-aware label.
Answer as JSON: {"acceptor": "SITE#k[i,j,k]"} (e.g. "O2#3[0,1,0]"; omit #1 and [0,0,0]).

options.acceptor: copy-aware label SITE#k[i,j,k]; 14 N/O sites, 4 operations

gold_method: Nearest N/O atom of another molecule to the home copy of the H over all operations and lattice shifts; copy-aware label = generating operation + shift from its wrapped copy (verified identical to MatterVis label_sym).
metric: partial: 0.2 x site label + 0.4 x operation index + 0.4 x lattice shift (score_v3); strict exact also reported

chance.note: score = 0.2 site + 0.4 operation + 0.4 shift; shift chance over 27 shifts

why_hard_from_cif_text: The answer is an exact symmetry-operation index and lattice shift. From text the model must apply every CIF operation (Z'>1 or 8 operations), wrap, scan neighbouring cells and compare dozens of N/O distances; chemistry priors (acid dimer = inversion, amide chain = translation) do not give the operation number or the shift. In the TUI the label_sym tag of the nearest N/O is printed next to the atom.
tui_path: TUI: label_sym + grow_radius 3 A shows the nearest N/O with its #k[i,j,k] tag next to the H.
mck_tool_path: mck library has per-contact H-bond detection (analysis/interactions/hydrogen_bond.py) but the CLI 'analyze interactions' only prints counts/scores: GAP = per-contact H-bond list with symmetry codes.
adhoc_tool_path: tools: geom_nearest_atoms(atom=H, elements=[N,O], other_molecules_only) or geom_hbond_list; TUI: show_hbonds overlay + distance action

tui_feasibility.reason: acceptor copy is in the scene with its label_sym tag (distance action available to compare candidates)

question:
Conventions. Atoms are named with copy-aware labels (as in the MatterVis TUI label_sym mode): SITE#k[i,j,k] is the copy of CIF site SITE generated by symmetry operation k (1-based, in the order of the CIF symmetry-operation list; '#k' is omitted for k = 1, i.e. x,y,z), wrapped into the unit cell [0,1) and then shifted by the lattice vector [i,j,k] ('[i,j,k]' is omitted for [0,0,0]). The home copy of a site is plain SITE (operation 1, wrapped into [0,1)). A molecule is a covalently bonded unit (bond: distance < sum of covalent radii + 0.45 A, + 0.30 A for X-H); ions and water molecules count as molecules. A hydrogen bond is D-H...A with D, A in {N, O}, H...A <= 2.50 A and angle D-H...A >= 120 deg.

Let M0 be the molecule containing the home copy of O1, and M1 the copy of M0 translated by the lattice vector [0,1,1] (M1 contains O1[0,1,1]). What is the minimum number of hydrogen bonds in a chain of molecules M0 -> ... -> M1, where consecutive molecules in the chain are joined by at least one hydrogen bond (any molecules and copies may be used)? If M1 cannot be reached from M0 through hydrogen bonds, answer "none".
Answer as JSON: {"hops": "<1-12 or none>"}.
gold_method: Breadth-first search over molecule instances in the molecular H-bond graph (all operations and shifts); answer unchanged with H...A 2.375/2.625 A and angle 114/126 deg.
metric: exact match
why_hard_from_cif_text: Needs the full molecular H-bond graph over symmetry and lattice copies and a breadth-first search (3-6 hops). Each hop requires finding the H-bond partner copy; errors compound and the minimum must be proven, not guessed.
tui_path: TUI: repeat 2x2x2 supercell + label_sym; follow H-bonds step by step (no H-bond lines drawn).
mck_tool_path: GAP: no mck command builds the molecular H-bond graph / shortest path between molecule copies.
adhoc_tool_path: tools: geom_hbond_path(atom, translation) -> chain of H-bonds (model counts the steps); TUI: show_hbonds overlay in a 2x2x2 supercell

tui_feasibility.reason: both M0 and its translate are inside the 2x2x2 supercell and labelled and the show_hbonds overlay draws/lists on-screen H-bonds, but the chain must be followed across views and intermediate molecules may be cut at the supercell edge

Consider the hydrogen bond O12-H12...O31 (home copies of O12 and H12; acceptor copy O31). Find the smallest closed ring that contains this hydrogen bond and is made only of covalent bonds and hydrogen bonds (a graph-set R ring). Count every atom in the ring, H atoms included, and count the distinct molecules (distinct copies) the ring passes through.
Answer as JSON: {"ring_size": <integer 4-48>, "n_molecules": <integer 1-12>}.
gold_method: Shortest cycle through the given H...A edge in the atom graph (covalent + H-bond edges) over all molecule copies within 4 H-bond hops; unique size/molecule count; unchanged under +-5 % H-bond criteria.

why_hard_from_cif_text: A graph-set ring of 12-36 atoms spanning 4-6 molecules must be traced through covalent bonds and H-bonds across several symmetry copies; the ring size is not stated and no textbook motif applies.
tui_path: TUI: grow_radius 9 A + label_sym; trace the ring atom by atom (no H-bond lines drawn).
mck_tool_path: GAP: no graph-set (R/C/D motif) analysis in mck CLI or library.
adhoc_tool_path: tools: geom_hbond_ring(h_atom, acceptor) -> ring members with their molecules (model counts atoms and molecules); TUI: show_hbonds overlay

tui_feasibility.reason: all 32 ring atoms are inside the grow_radius scene with label_sym tags, but tracing a 32-atom ring through overlay-listed H-bonds in 100x36 ASCII is hard

This structure is disordered: some sites belong to disorder groups (_atom_site_disorder_group / PART) with partial occupancy. Build two ordered models. MAJOR keeps every site without a disorder group plus the disorder group(s) with the higher occupancy; MINOR keeps every site without a disorder group plus the disorder group(s) with the lower occupancy. In each model, count the OTHER molecules (all symmetry copies and lattice translates; ions and solvent included) that have at least one atom within 4.1 A of any atom of the reference molecule (in MAJOR the molecule containing the home copy of F1, in MINOR the molecule containing the home copy of O1?).

why_hard_from_cif_text: The model must split sites by PART / occupancy, build two ordered replicas, expand each and count neighbour molecules inside a cutoff. Requires the disorder columns of the CIF and a full neighbour search, twice.
tui_path: TUI: shows both disorder components (minor ones flagged) with labels; ordered replicas must be imagined.
